Definition: to groan, i.e. bewail; hence (through the idea of crying aloud), to assemble (as if on proclamation)
BiblicalUsage: Nahah means to groan or bewail, to cry aloud in grief, and it is used for a nation lamenting and for a prophet wailing. In 1 Samuel 7:2 all the house of Israel lamented after the Lord while the ark abode in Kirjath-jearim for twenty years, and in Ezekiel 32:18 the son of man is told to wail for the multitude of Egypt and cast them down to the pit.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that lamenting after the Lord is the beginning of return, because Israel's grief in 1 Samuel 7:2 is what brought Samuel back to lead them; grief that turns toward God is not despair; it is prayer.
